transcript.text: An oven that 'won't come on' can mean either no power to the unit at all, or no heat despite the controls being active. The most common cause for a sudden stop is actually a control state issue: after a brief power flicker or if an end-time was set, many ovens default into 'Auto' mode where they wait for the clock to be set before allowing heat. First, check if any lights or numbers appear on the display when you switch it on. If the clock is flashing or you see a timer symbol, try setting the current time and switching the function knob to Manual (often indicated by a hand symbol) rather than leaving it in Auto.
display is flashing 0.00 and a little symbol. there was a power cut last night. how do i set the clock?

To set the clock, look for buttons labelled 'Clock', 'Timer', or a 'Menu' key on your control panel. Press 'Clock', then use the '+' and '-' (or arrow) keys to adjust the time, and press 'Start' or 'OK' to confirm. Once the correct time is displayed, turn the function knob to Manual (often marked with a hand symbol) rather than Auto, as many ovens will not heat in Auto mode until the clock is set.
ok but which buttons? i dont have the manual. its a neff

For Neff ovens without a manual, try this: Press the 'Clock' button (sometimes you need to hold it for 3 seconds), then use the '+' and '-' buttons to set the correct time. Press 'Start' or 'OK' to confirm. Once the clock is set, turn the function knob to Manual (usually marked with a hand symbol) rather than leaving it in Auto. If the oven still doesn't heat after this, please let me know if any lights or numbers appear on the display when you switch it on.
there's no button marked clock, just symbols. which one do i press? it still shows flashing 0.00

The flashing 0.00 is the clock resetting after the power cut; it's not an error code. On many Neff models, you need to press and hold the button with a clock symbol (often at the top right) for about 3 seconds until the digits start blinking or change. If there isn't one, try pressing 'Menu' or 'Settings'. Once the time is set, turn the function knob to Manual (hand symbol). If that doesn't work, let me know which buttons are present.
no menu or settings, just a row of symbols. which one is the clock? one looks like a little clock, one is a key, one is a plus and minus

The button that looks like a little clock is the one you need. Press and hold it for about 3 seconds until the '0.00' starts flashing or changes. Then use the plus (+) and minus (-) buttons to set the correct time, and press Start (or OK) to confirm. Once the time is set, turn the function knob to Manual (often marked with a hand symbol). Many Neff ovens will not heat until this is done after a power cut.
ok pressed and held the clock one, set the time, and it came on and heated. thanks

That's excellent news. To stop this from happening again after a power cut, just remember to turn the function knob to Manual (the hand symbol) once you've set the time; otherwise it will stay in Auto mode and refuse to heat until the clock is updated.
